description: Ayanamsha across the precession cycle for every mode the API exposes. Underpins every sidereal longitude the engine publishes.

source.authority: Swiss Ephemeris 2.10.03 (DE441) evaluated against a mathematical definition
source.definition: Ayanamsha is the angular offset between the tropical and sidereal zodiacs at an instant: sidereal_longitude = tropical_longitude - ayanamsha. Each named mode (Lahiri, Raman, Krishnamurti, True Citra) is a distinct published definition of where the sidereal zero point sits, so there is no single universal truth - the mode is part of the question.
source.method: swe.get_ayanamsa_ex_ut(jd, FLG_SWIEPH) via tests/golden/definitions.py::ayanamsha. Deliberately the _ex_ variant: get_ayanamsa_ut disagrees by 6-18 arcsec and does NOT match what FLG_SIDEREAL applies. See docs/ayanamsha-variants.md.
source.convention: UT timescale. Values are the ayanamsha swisseph applies under FLG_SIDEREAL for the named mode, which is what the engine's planets use.
source.verified_by: Cross-checked against the engine's own default_engine.ayanamsa() after the unification; agreement to 1e-9 deg.
source.notes: Spans 3000 BCE to 3000 CE, ~1/4 of the 25,772-year precession cycle, covering the range the shipped .se1 files support.

tolerance.rationale: Ayanamsha is a smooth analytic function of time for every mode here, so agreement should be near-exact; 1 arcsec detects a formula, epoch-convention or variant change (the ex_ut/_ut split is 6-18 arcsec, comfortably caught) while tolerating float noise.
